questions.question: Maya's granola bar is cut into 8 equal pieces, and she eats 4 of those pieces. Which sentence names exactly the same amount of that same bar?
options: 4/8 of the bar, which is the same amount as 1/2 of the bar
1/2 of the whole box that holds 4 of those granola bars
1/4 of the bar, because she ate 4 pieces
1/2 of her sister's granola bar, which is twice as long
questions.explain: Divide the top and bottom of 4/8 by 4 to get 1/2, so 4 of the 8 pieces is half of that bar. The trap is taking half of something else (a whole box, or a bigger bar) — equivalent fractions only match when they are parts of the same whole.

questions.question: A metre stick is marked into 10 equal parts. Kira's ribbon stretches along 5 of those parts, so the ribbon is 5/10 of a metre long. Which piece of string is exactly the same length as her ribbon?
options: A string that is 1/2 of a 2 m rope
A string that is 1/2 of a metre
A string that is 1/5 of a metre
A string that is 5/10 of a 2 m rope
questions.explain: 5 of 10 equal parts is 5/10, and dividing both numbers by 5 gives 1/2, so the ribbon is half a metre. The trap is taking 1/2 of a 2 m rope — that is half of a different whole, so it comes out to a whole metre instead.

questions.question: Noah's measuring cup is divided into 4 equal parts. He fills it up to the 3rd part, so he has 3/4 of a cup of rolled oats. Which amount is exactly the same as what is in his cup?
options: 4/5 of a cup
3/4 of a 2-cup jug
6/8 of a cup
3/8 of a cup
questions.explain: Multiply both the numerator and the denominator of 3/4 by 2 to get 6/8, the same amount cut into smaller pieces. Two traps: adding 1 to the top and bottom (that gives 4/5, which is not equivalent), and taking 3/4 of a bigger 2-cup jug, which is a different whole and a much larger amount.

questions.question: A chocolate bar is made of 12 equal squares. Priya breaks off 3 squares for herself. Which fraction of that same bar is equal to the part she took?
options: 1/3 of the bar
1/4 of the party-size bar that has 24 squares
3/4 of the bar
1/4 of the bar
questions.explain: Priya took 3/12 of the bar, and dividing both numbers by 3 gives 1/4 of that bar. Watch out for 1/4 of the bigger 24-square bar — that is a quarter of a different whole, so it is 6 squares, not 3.

questions.question: Jonah has 3/4 of a metre of ribbon for a craft project. His measuring tape is marked only in twelfths of a metre. Which mark on the tape shows exactly the same length as his ribbon?
questions.explain: To turn fourths into twelfths, multiply the denominator by 3, so multiply the numerator by 3 as well: 3/4 = 9/12. The trap is keeping the 3 on top and only changing the bottom, which gives 3/12 — that is just a quarter of a metre.

questions.question: At soccer practice, 6 of the team's 10 water bottles are full. Which of these describes exactly the same amount of that team's bottles?
options: 3/5 of a crate of 20 bottles
3/5 of the bottles
3/10 of the bottles
2/5 of the bottles
questions.explain: Divide both 6 and 10 by 2 to get 3/5, so 6 out of 10 bottles is three-fifths of the team's bottles. The trap is using the same fraction on a different whole: 3/5 of a crate of 20 is 12 bottles, not 6.

questions.question: Dev poured 5/10 of a litre of milk and wants to write that same amount using halves of a litre. Which step correctly gives an equivalent fraction?
options: Divide only the denominator by 5, giving 5/2 L
Subtract 5 from the top and from the bottom, giving 0/5 L
Divide both the numerator and the denominator by 5, giving 1/2 L
Divide only the numerator by 5, giving 1/10 L
questions.explain: An equivalent fraction keeps the same amount, so you must multiply or divide the numerator and the denominator by the same number: 5/10 divided by 5 on both parts is 1/2. Changing just one part, or subtracting instead of dividing, changes the actual amount of milk.

questions.question: At a birthday party, 8 of the 12 cupcakes on the tray have sprinkles. Which of these describes exactly the same amount of that tray's cupcakes?
options: 2/3 of a party pack of 24 cupcakes
1/3 of the cupcakes
2/12 of the cupcakes
2/3 of the cupcakes
questions.explain: Divide both 8 and 12 by 4 to get 2/3, so 8 of the 12 cupcakes is two-thirds of the tray. The traps: 2/3 of a 24-cupcake party pack is 16 cupcakes — the same fraction of a different whole; 1/3 counts the 4 plain cupcakes instead of the sprinkled ones; and 2/12 divides only the numerator, which changes the amount.

questions.question: At a family dinner, Ben cuts a large pizza into 4 equal slices and eats 1 slice. Emma cuts a small personal pizza into 2 equal pieces and eats 1 piece. Ben says: 'I definitely ate less, because 1/4 is always smaller than 1/2.' Which statement is correct?
options: Ben is right — 1/4 is always less than 1/2, no matter how big each pizza is
Ben is right, because his pizza was cut into 4 pieces and hers into only 2
Ben is wrong, because 1/4 and 1/2 are equivalent fractions
Ben cannot be sure — 1/4 and 1/2 can only be compared fairly when they are parts of the same-size whole, and his pizza is much larger than Emma's
questions.explain: Fractions only compare directly when the whole is the same size, so a quarter of a large pizza can easily be more food than half of a small personal pizza. Also remember 1/4 and 1/2 are not equivalent — 1/2 is the same as 2/4.

questions.question: Zoe needs 3/4 of a cup of vegetable oil for a cake, but the only scoop in the drawer holds 1/8 of a cup. How many full scoops of oil does she need?
options: 6 scoops
3 scoops
8 scoops
12 scoops
questions.explain: First rename the amount in eighths: multiply both parts of 3/4 by 2 to get 6/8, so she needs 6 scoops of 1/8 cup. The trap is reading only the 3 on top and taking 3 scoops, which would give just 3/8 of a cup — half of what the recipe needs.

questions.question: Ravi and Mia each bought a 500 mL bottle of juice, and the two bottles are exactly the same size. Ravi drank 2/5 of his bottle and Mia drank 4/10 of hers. Who drank more juice?
options: Mia, because 4/10 of a litre is more than 2/5 of 500 mL
Neither — 2/5 and 4/10 are equivalent, and the bottles are the same size, so they each drank the same 200 mL
Mia, because 4 parts is more than 2 parts
Ravi, because fifths are bigger pieces than tenths, so 2/5 must be more
questions.explain: Multiply both parts of 2/5 by 2 to get 4/10, so the two fractions name the same share, and since both bottles hold 500 mL each child drank 200 mL. The trap is switching the whole partway through — comparing a fraction of a litre with a fraction of a 500 mL bottle is not a fair comparison.

questions.question: At a school bake sale, the first tray holds 8 equal squares of banana bread and 6 of them are sold. The second tray is twice as big: it holds 16 equal squares, and 12 of them are sold. Which statement is true?
options: The first tray sold a bigger fraction, because eighths are bigger pieces than sixteenths
The second tray sold a bigger fraction, because 12 squares sold is more than 6 squares sold
The same fraction — 3/4 — was sold from each tray, but the second tray sold more squares because its whole is bigger
Both trays sold 3/4, so both trays sold the same number of squares
questions.explain: 6/8 and 12/16 both simplify to 3/4, so the same fraction of each tray was sold, but 3/4 of a bigger tray is a bigger number of squares (12 instead of 6). Equal fractions mean equal amounts only when the wholes are the same size.
